audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty advice credits Kassadin with a 'sidestep tool' pre-6 and tells you to 'save W to block his dive path' after 6, when Riftwalk is a 500-range blink that ignores terrain.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Kassadin teleports to a nearby location.' A teleport is not a dash, so Crystallize cannot deny it — the tldr already says so and the do's contradict it.
audit.corrected: Pre-6 he has no mobility at all and a 400-range Force Pulse; post-6 the wall cuts his walk-back path and his access to the wave, never the blink itself.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart disagrees between layers: phases[0..3].side and phases[5].side read 'Skill' and phases[6].side reads 'Kassadin', while win[0..6] are all 'Anivia' and packet.levelChart is all 'Anivia'.
audit.why: Two layers render two different answers to the same row, and the full layer even hands the last row to Kassadin against a 52.08% Anivia win rate and its own prose ('this matchup stays lopsided in your favor throughout').
audit.corrected: All seven phases[N].side = Anivia, matching win[0..6] and the packet chart. Real spikes: Anivia at Lost Chapter and level 6; Kassadin at Riftwalk rank-ups (5s to 3.5s to 2s) and his first mana item.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three decisive interactions are absent: Null Sphere's shield absorbs magic damage (your entire kit), Void Stone reduces magic damage taken, and Force Pulse charges from spells cast in his vicinity — including your own.
audit.why: Riot's text for Q states the excess energy 'grants a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage'; the passive states he 'takes reduced magic damage'; E states he 'draws energy from spells cast in his vicinity'. All three change how you spend Q, E and gold, and none of them reach the page.
audit.corrected: Bait Null Sphere out before committing burst. Buy Void Staff earlier than usual because Void Stone taxes every point of your damage. Do not free-cast beside him — your own Glacial Storm ticks charge Force Pulse.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects flags no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere; breakdown.cooldowns carries no numbers.
audit.why: The sequencing that decides this lane is numeric: Force Pulse is 21s at rank 1, Null Sphere 9s, Riftwalk 5s at rank 1 falling to 2s at rank 3.
audit.corrected: Step up on Force Pulse's 21s downtime; commit only after Null Sphere's shield is spent; understand that Riftwalk's cooldown shortens rather than being 'waited out' late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization never mentions magic penetration despite Void Stone.
audit.why: Anivia deals no physical damage; a flat magic-damage reduction passive is the single biggest itemization lever in this matchup.
audit.corrected: Void Staff is not situational here.

audit.whatIsWrong: The brief's derived flag marks Null Sphere as 'channel: interruptible' and the missingInteractions entry claims Flash Frost cancels it.
audit.why: Riot's own description says Null Sphere is a point-and-click orb that interrupts channels — it is not itself a channel. The flag is a tooltip-parsing misfire and the claim would be a fabricated interaction.
audit.corrected: Do not write that your Q cancels Null Sphere. Write instead that Null Sphere interrupts channels, so a recall started inside his 650 range gets cancelled.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Crystallize for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Riftwalk: 5s at rank 1 and it is a blink, so Crystallize never stops it — kill him before it ranks to 2s. - Force Pulse: 21s at rank 1, 400 range; stay outside the cone and he has nothing. - Null Sphere: 9s, and its shield eats magic.

edits.before: If Kassadin opens the score, reset expectations and respect Riftwalk doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with R wave-clear and stay relevant through zone control.
edits.after: If Kassadin gets the first kill he reaches his item threshold early, so stop contesting and shove with R. After a second, ward both rivers — a fed Riftwalk reaches you from 500 straight through your own wave.

edits.before: Carry by controlling space — storm and wall decide where fights happen, and your stun decides who dies first inside them.
edits.after: Carry by out-ranging the blink: 500 range means he has to arrive beside you, and a Q the instant he lands is a stun plus a doubled E.

edits.before: Ahead, the lane is a prison: storm every wave, wall Kassadin away from the comeback farm, and rotate first to every river fight with your stun loaded.
edits.after: Ahead, starve the scaling: shove with R, deny the wave that feeds him Nether Blade mana, and take his side camps before he can farm back to items.

edits.before: - Anivia vs Kassadin - Track: Kassadin Riftwalk. - Hold Q for his engage — never spend the stun on poke. - Fights start when Riftwalk ends. - The R is for endings, not openings.
edits.after: - Anivia vs Kassadin - Track: Riftwalk, a 500-range blink the wall cannot stop. - Bait Null Sphere's magic shield before you commit. - Stay outside his 400 Force Pulse cone.

edits.before: His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Riftwalk is only 500 range; a wave held near your tower means he has to spend two blinks to reach you.

edits.before: Kassadin whiffs Riftwalk and the lane briefly belongs to you.

edits.after: His second Riftwalk costs more mana but deals more damage — chasing means eating both blinks with your Q already spent.

edits.after: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Lost Chapter into Rod of Ages or Seraph's; Void Staff is mandatory here — Void Stone cuts all your magic damage. Zhonya's vs dive.

edits.after: First item is yours — Seraph's keeps Storm running while he still needs two more items

notes: Six-row level-chart fix proposed as one atomic group; the content layer (win[0..6], all Anivia) already matches the packet chart, so the full layer is the one being corrected and no paired content edit exists. Flag misfire recorded: the brief marks Null Sphere with 'channel: interruptible' and missingInteractions claims Flash Frost cancels it, but Riot's description says Null Sphere INTERRUPTS channels rather than being one — no such claim written. The content layer repeatedly calls Kassadin 'mana-starved'; Nether Blade restores mana on a 7s cooldown, so that framing is overstated, but the lines were left alone rather than rewritten on an unverified magnitude.
